heightEncoding.note: Step is fitted to this interior's own vertical range, so the six-bit field spans it without clamping. The Godot loader still takes elevation from the rendered Walk_ surfaces; this grid is authoritative only for walkability.

cutaway.reason: interior lids; the isometric rig frames the floor, not the roof

notes: Every standable surface is a Walk_<material> node, matching the region's contract: the client turns navigation.surfaceNodePrefixes into the layer its downward grounding ray tests.

sections.name: The Resonant Vault
notes: Dressed slate and brass throughout, against the ochre dust of the region above: the Glasswardens built down away from the storm.
The gallery walkways are scenery, not walk surfaces. They are reachable from nowhere, and marking them walkable would let the grounding ray stand an actor two metres above the bench floor.

sections.name: The Geode Hollow
notes: No dressed stone and no brass anywhere in this package. It is the one interior that is not built, only entered, and it earns its place by being unlike the other three.
The crystal lining is placed on a radial falloff, so shards are dense against the walls and thin over the floor a player actually crosses.

sections.name: The Shardworks
notes: The headframe is open to the sky, so the shaft reads as a hole in the barrens rather than as a door in a wall.
Warm timber and iron against cold crystal is the whole point: this is the only interior of the four where people are working.

sections.name: The Storm Barrow
notes: The strike well is the one space in these four interiors with no lid: it is open to the region's sky, and the storm is what is still using this room.
Coarse rubble and unadorned ashlar only. Nothing here is Glasswarden work, and no brass appears until the Vault.

sections.name: The Sour Cut
notes: Built from the shared small-room kit: mouth, throat and chamber, dressed for the region above it.

sections.name: The Measure House
notes: Built from the shared small-room kit: a cut sanctuary in the crystal manner.

sections.name: The Shard Counter's House
notes: Built from the shared small-room kit: a hall with a hearth and a back room for its trade (workshop).

interactives.name: The Shard Focus
interactives.label: A seam of crystal that hums at a touch; the rock behind it is thin.

provenance.geometry: authored with the shared Nymara toolkit; no scattered placement

notes: Four interiors on one map with blackspace between them, in the Eternal Lands convention: one GLB, one manifest, one collision grid, one server map key, and an arrival point per surface door.

The blackspace is not drawn. The collision grid is built only where a Walk_ surface exists, so the gutters between sections are blocked by construction rather than by a mask that could drift out of step.
Sections are spaced so no two come within about forty metres, which is what keeps one section's lamps and cameras out of the next.
knownLimitations: Not opened in Godot: no client is installable in the build environment, so collision response, navmesh generation, portal transition, LOD and transparency sorting are unverified.
eloria-server has not registered these map keys.
